(a) Since you enjoy weekend cycling, you could plan a kitchen project inspired by the places you’ve biked to—like making energy bars from scratch or crafting homemade electrolyte drinks. You could also explore dehydrating fruits or making your own granola mixes for your next ride. This way, your food prep becomes part of your cycling routine.
(b) You could try making fresh pasta by hand, experimenting with different shapes and sauces to pair with it. Another enjoyable option is creating homemade jams or preserves from seasonal fruits. If you’re feeling adventurous, crafting decorative cupcakes or layered cakes can be a fun, hands-on challenge.
(c) Given your Midwestern roots, you might enjoy trying out hearty comfort foods like homemade pot pies or casseroles with fresh, locally sourced vegetables. Another project could be perfecting your own apple pie from scratch, using a flaky butter crust. You could also try pickling vegetables—a tradition with deep ties to regional home cooking.
(d) Since you already enjoy baking bread from scratch, you could experiment with naturally leavened breads using different grains, or even try shaping intricate braided challahs. Another fun option is filling dough with seasonal fruits or savory ingredients for a unique twist on your usual loaves. You might also enjoy building your own sourdough starter variations to compare flavor profiles over time.
